answer: Stop sybil farms with a one-chip-one-agent registry. First, each agent creates its identity key inside a secure enclave chip that never exports it. Second, every epoch the chip signs a fresh nonce, proving the same hardware is alive at dawn. Third, the registry rejects any second identity sharing a chip fingerprint, while peers audit a random 5% sample weekly. Forging 10,000 agents then needs 10,000 chips at $45 each, $450,000 of hardware and 200 hours. No fable of a thousand soldiers from one shadow survives here: this haven admits one keeper per lamp, and one lamp per keeper.
